Commentary.Commentary: That is all from this game. Jaker Ali collects the trophy and joins his teammates for the victory celebration. A complete performance from Bangladesh and they can build on this series. Worrying signs for Afghanistan in the T20I circuit, but they don't have much time to ponder, as the ODI series is underway in a couple of days. The three-match ODI series kicks off at the Sheikh Zayed Stadium, Abu Dhabi, on the 8th of October. Join us at 10 am GMT and earlier for the build-up. Till then, cheers!

Jaker Ali, the captain of Bangladesh, says the players came back well after a disappointing Asia Cup. Tells that they have done a good job as a fielding side but so have the bowling and batting departments. Reckons the players are capable but need to believe and be more confident. Mentions before this series, they prepared a lot and he is happy with how the bunch has performed.

Rashid Khan, the skipper of Afghanistan! Starts by saying they played bad cricket and Bangladesh played outstanding cricket in all departments. Believes they were beaten 3-0 due to the poor effort in the field. Feels they haven't shown the intent they are famous for and feels they were defensive cricket in the past few series. Shares they need to work with the top order, as he feels the middle order has the firepower to put on a big score. Mentions there is no doubt about the skill but it's about the frame of mind going into the game and feels that is more important. Tells Bashir Ahmad and Abdullah Ahmadzai have done well in the domestic circuit, they have potential but need more opportunities and more time.

Nasum Ahmed wins the PLAYER OF THE SERIES AWARD. He says he has done well against New Zealand and Australia, as well as at home. Reckons the pitch was on the slower side and he used his variation and whatever was on offer.

Saif Hassan wins the PLAYER OF THE MATCH AWARD. He is happy to contribute to the team and hopes the team rides the momentum. Tells that for the last 2-3 months, he has been trying to play in this manner. Reckons the coach gave him a clear plan in this series and that helped him.
Presentation...

While their batters struggled, Afghanistan relied on their experienced bowlers and they delivered. However, Bashir Ahmad and Abdullah Ahmadzai went for plenty in a low-scoring game, which ultimately toppled their chances of avoiding a clean sweep. Credit to Bangladesh. They showed intent with the bat, not just in this game but throughout the series. The openers, after the first-match success, struggled in the next two games but with a moderate total to chase, Bangladesh needed someone to anchor the innings and Saif Hassan came to the fore. Losing Jaker Ali and Shamim Hossain in consecutive deliveries put some pressure on Bangladesh but Saif Hassan showed good match awareness to hang in there and see the game off with a fine fifty to his name.

On a pitch that was on the slower side and had ample turn in it, Afghanistan managed just two wickets off their spinners. Only Mujeeb Ur Rahman was in the wickets column while Rashid Khan failed to pick up any wickets, and Mohammad Nabi wasn't used. However, we can't blame it on the Afghan bowlers as their batters once again fumbled to put on a score. In every game in the series, their batters struggled and today, the case was same.

A calm, composed innings from Saif Hassan has ensured a famous whitewash against Afghanistan. A complete performance from Bangladesh once again and they have deservingly hammered Afghanistan in this series.

Commentary.Commentary: Wide! Mujeeb Ur Rahman errs and bowls it way over the tramline, left alone.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Mujeeb Ur Rahman to Tanzid Hasan, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Flat and targeting the top of off, Hasan punches it to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Mujeeb Ur Rahman to Tanzid Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Very full and on middle and off, Parvez Hossain Emon sweeps it to deep square leg for a single.

Commentary.Commentary: Tossed up on middle, nudged to mid-wicket.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Parvez Hossain Emon was itching to score one! Gets it in the slot, around off, Parvez Hossain Emon slog-sweeps it over long on for a biggie. First boundary of the chase.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Mujeeb Ur Rahman to Parvez Hossain Emon, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: This is brilliant stuff from Azmatullah Omarzai! Short in length and around off, lands and nips away. Hasan is drawn to defend but is well beaten.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Azmatullah Omarzai to Tanzid Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Azmatullah Omarzai keeps it tight around off with a fuller delivery, Hasan punches it to mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Azmatullah Omarzai to Tanzid Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Parvez Hossain Emon is finally underway! Sharp single! Outside off, Parvez Hossain Emon crunches it to cover where the fielder dives to his right and stops it for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Azmatullah Omarzai to Parvez Hossain Emon, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Touch fuller and on middle and leg, Parvez Hossain Emon lofts it off the inner half to mid on where Rashid Khan stops on a bounce.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Azmatullah Omarzai to Parvez Hossain Emon, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Another dot! Parvez Hossain Emon is hurrying here! Goes after the short ball with a slash but fails to connect.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Azmatullah Omarzai to Parvez Hossain Emon, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Wide! Bowls it outside off and it swings away, it is left alone.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Azmatullah Omarzai to Parvez Hossain Emon, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Hasan and Bangladesh are underway! Pitches it up front, outside off. Hasan drives it to mid off for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Azmatullah Omarzai to Tanzid Hasan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Azmatullah Omarzai to bowl from the other end.
Yes, he can! A maiden to start the chase! Tossed up on middle, Parvez Hossain Emon leans and defends.

Commentary.Commentary: Another dot! Flat and outside off, a bit slower. Parvez Hossain Emon slaps it straight to cover. Can Mujeeb Ur Rahman end with a maiden?
